property_summary: For any caller, if a transferOwnership call does not revert, the owner must have been the previous owner or the new owner.
After any successful call to transferOwnership(newOwner), the owner must equal the original owner before the call or newOwner; the bug allows anyone to set owner arbitrarily, violating this.

After any call to transferOwnership completes without reverting, the new owner must have been set through a previous legitimate ownership transfer originating from the contract deployment. The bug allows any address to become owner directly, breaking this invariant.
For any non-zero new owner, after a call to transferOwnership, the owner should change to the new owner; the buggy version always leaves the owner unchanged.
After any valid call to transferOwnership with a non-zero new owner where the caller is the current owner, the correct contract updates owner to the new address, while the buggy version reverts.
For any caller and any new owner address, a call to transferOwnership(newOwner) from the current owner should succeed; the buggy version always reverts regardless of caller or new owner.

For any caller that is the current owner and any new owner address, after a call to transferOwnership(newOwner) the owner must equal newOwner if the call succeeds (does not revert); the buggy version always reverts, so the owner never changes.

For any caller, after a non-reverting call to transferOwnership, the owner must equal either the caller (if the caller is the current owner) or the old owner; the buggy version always reverts so the owner is never the caller.

A call to owned() must succeed (not revert) when called by the contract owner; the bug sets owner to address(0) at the start of owned(), which causes the onlyOwner modifier to revert when called by any owner.

After any sequence of calls, if owned() succeeds for the current owner, the owner variable must remain unchanged; the bug sets owner to address(0) during owned(), so a successful call by a non-zero owner changes owner to zero.
For any caller, calling owned() must leave the owner variable unchanged; the bug sets owner to address(0) during owned(), violating that invariant.

For any caller, if owned() succeeds (does not revert), then the caller must be the owner; the bug sets owner to address(0) inside owned(), so a successful call implies the caller was owner before the call but owner becomes 0 afterward, yet the rule only checks the precondition.
After a successful call to owned() by any caller, the owner must remain unchanged; the bug sets owner to address(0) inside owned(), so a successful call changes owner to zero.
For any caller, a call to owned() should revert if that caller is not the owner; the mutated version removes this requirement so it never reverts for any non-owner caller.
For any caller, if the caller is not the owner, a call to owned() should revert; the buggy version never reverts.
For any caller that is not the owner, a call to owned() must revert, but the buggy version omits the onlyOwner modifier so it succeeds for non-owner callers.
